name: Pale Aqua
lede: Pale Aqua is a soft, greyed blue first fixed by the ISCC-NBS 1955 color charts, and one of the most common light blues in our painting archive.

sections.title: A modifier, charted in 1955
sections.body:
The library's earliest source for Pale Aqua is the ISCC-NBS 1955 charts, where it sits in the "very pale green" block; Wikipedia separately cites the Plochere system, and the xkcd 2010 survey recorded the name again as a crowd label [1]. It is built on the modifier grammar *pale* + *aqua*, so [[aqua|Aqua]] itself is the more saturated color this one lightens [1]. At hex #BED3E5 it measures lightness 84 and chroma just 12 in LCH, close to grey [1].

Its nearest named neighbors are [[columbia-blue|Columbia Blue]], 3.6 CIEDE2000 units off and bluer, and [[cloudy-blue|Cloudy Blue]], 4.6 units off and darker; [[pastel-blue|Pastel Blue]] sits 5.8 units off, bluer and darker [2]. The library separately logs Beau Blue as a near-duplicate, just 1.0 unit away [1]. A treated "sky" blue [[gem:topaz|topaz]] sits 7.9 units off, and the color shows up again in the hand-painted skies of [[film:the-grand-budapest-hotel|The Grand Budapest Hotel]], 4.8 units away [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pale blue in 121 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.51%, as photographed, more common than 56% of the named colors here [4]. The earliest match is a 1450 painting by Andrea del Castagno, 505 years before the ISCC-NBS charts fixed the name, which only shows an aged photograph can resemble this hue, not that anyone named it so early, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 13 of 1,674 paintings, at 1.7 times the archive's overall rate, and inside a painting it most often plays a light, in 58% of its matches [4]. John Singer Sargent carries it in 4 of his 287 works here, 3.1 times the baseline [4].
